intended_object: A type with an order relation and an infimum operator `sInf : Set α → α` that returns a greatest lower bound of `s` whenever `s` has one. This comes from the docstring and from the dual class `OrderSupSet`.
explanation:
The class extends `InfSet α` and adds one axiom: whenever some `a` is a greatest lower bound of `s` (`IsGLB s a`), `sInf s` is also a greatest lower bound of `s`. This is exactly what the docstring says: `sInf` gives a greatest lower bound whenever one exists. It places no condition on sets with no greatest lower bound, so `sInf` can take any value there, which is the usual junk-value convention.

It is stated for an arbitrary `[LE α]`, which is the most general setting where `IsGLB` makes sense. When `≤` is not antisymmetric, a set can have several greatest lower bounds, and the axiom only asks that `sInf s` be one of them, which is the right requirement. Being a greatest lower bound in Lean's sense also implies being a lower bound, so the axiom carries no hidden extra condition.

Nothing in Mathlib is more general than this class, and it is the dual of `OrderSupSet` (linked by `to_dual`). So the definition is faithful.
